sections.content: You know *usted* commands from A2 Unit 23 (*pase*, *firme*), the subjunctive after requests from B1 Unit 4 and *rogar* from B1 Unit 38. In forms, notices and letters, Spanish often avoids the plain command. Three formal patterns are worth knowing.

*Le ruego que* + present subjunctive: "I ask you to…". *Sírvase* + infinitive: "kindly…", a formal way to give an instruction. *Le agradecería que* + imperfect subjunctive: "I would be grateful if you…". The first two are used in writing and on formal occasions; the third sounds polite in speech too.

sections.title: Formal ways to ask
rows: I ask you to sign here.
Le agradecería que me enviara el documento.
I would be grateful if you sent me the document.
Come in, take a seat, please.

sections.content: After *le ruego que* the verb is subjunctive (*firme*, not *firma*), as after any request. *Sírvase* is already a command, so it is followed directly by an infinitive: *sírvase esperar*.
